summary: The south-end light on Calumet Harbor's detached breakwater: a steel tower built at Holland, Michigan, moved here in 1937 and worked from the breakwater lighthouse.

structures.note: Built 1907 as the north pierhead light at Holland, Michigan; moved to Calumet 1937; Rowlett gives 45 ft (13.5 m) square steel skeletal tower (no height stated); lantern removed; solar-powered light shown from the top

access.note: Accessible only by boat; site and tower closed. Not open to the public (USLHS).

corrections.proposed: Position of USCG 7-19800 at the east/southeast end of the detached breakwater (not in the sources read; take it from the Light List)
corrections.why: The record's coordinates match the 1906 light at the end of the attached (older) breakwater (LighthouseFriends map: 41.72604, -87.49336; Rowlett's entry for USCG 7-19830). The name, USCG 7-19800 and the Holland tower describe the detached breakwater's far-end light.
1905 is Rowlett's 'station established' date for the attached breakwater light (USCG 7-19830). This light was commissioned 4 June 1937 (LighthouseFriends).

corrections.proposed: remove; these belong to the attached breakwater light
corrections.why: Rowlett dates the 1905 establishment and the 1995 tower to the attached breakwater light; LighthouseFriends says the 1995 tower replaced the old breakwater lighthouse.

corrections.current: 41 deg 72.60 min N, 87 deg 49.30 min W (USLHS place record)
corrections.why: The archive's coordinates, read as decimal degrees, put the record about 60 km from this light; the minutes look mistranscribed. Do not use it as a position.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's coordinates are the attached-breakwater light's; the south-end light is the detached breakwater's far-end tower (Rowlett, USCG 7-19800; LighthouseFriends, Holland tower). Position for 7-19800 not in the sources read.

Three dates: 1935 (USLHS establishment), 4 June 1937 (LighthouseFriends commissioning), and Rowlett's 1905 for the attached light. The story gives the 1937 commissioning and reports the archive's 1935.

notes_for_editor: IDENTITY. The name, the USCG number 7-19800 (Rowlett) and the relocated Holland tower all describe the light at the far end of the detached breakwater (commissioned 4 June 1937). The record's coordinates, its 1905 first-light date and its 1995 'Tower 2' belong to the light at the end of the older, attached breakwater (USCG 7-19830, Rowlett's 'Calumet Harbor'; LighthouseFriends' 'Calumet Harbor Lighthouse', demolished and replaced in 1995). I checked the Calumet Harbor records in data/stations (entrance north side, entrance south side, pierhead): none is the attached-breakwater light, so that light may need its own record. The editor should decide which light this id means. The story follows the name, the number and the Holland tower. POSITION. No coordinates are proposed: the Light List entry for 7-19800 was not read. CHARACTERISTIC. The record's Fl R 10s (ENC) disagrees with Rowlett's 'flash every 5 s, alternately red and white'; unresolved, check the Light List. FOG SIGNAL. Rowlett gives a fog horn; the USLHS form says 'Fog Signal Building? No'; LighthouseFriends calls the relocated tower a light and fog signal tower; unresolved. KEEPERS. None of its own; the USLHS place page lists no people. LighthouseFriends says the light was worked from the breakwater lighthouse; no keeper is assigned here. EAST OR SOUTHEAST. Rowlett says east end; LighthouseFriends says southeast end; both describe the far end. DATES. 1935 (USLHS) and 1937 (LighthouseFriends) differ; the 1937 commissioning is the best-sourced date. The 1966 automation and the 1995 demolition in the story belong to the breakwater lighthouse that worked this light; they are given as context only. STORMS AND RESCUES. Nothing in the sources ties a storm, wreck or rescue to this light. The Bulletin and Commissioner entries for Calumet Harbor (1912-1932: the Robinson and Osby rescues, the 1921 gale, the 1929 storms, the 1930 riprap) concern the attached breakwater light; they belong to that station's story. The corpus Bulletins for 1934-1939 do not mention the 1937 commissioning in their OCR. The story is short on purpose. Newspaper search for 1934-1937 returned nothing. The LighthouseFriends keeper roster (about eighty names, 1906-1966: breakwater head, first, second and third assistants, Coast Guard crew) belongs to the attached-breakwater light, not to this id; it is not transcribed here. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the Commissioner sentence is on scan p. 573 (printed p. 75, estimate No. 18 of the 1920 report; confirmed with corpus.py page); the OCR of that page reads 'about 2 .300', and the same sentence in the 1921 report (scan p. 678) reads 2,300, so 2,300 is taken as the figure. The USLHS place record answers 'Active Aid to Navigation? No' while Rowlett lists the light as active; both are now stated in Today. Rowlett gives 45 ft (13.5 m) for the square steel skeletal tower without saying whether it is the height, so height_m was removed. The story now says the Commissioner's 1920 annual report (not 'in 1920'), states the 600-foot gap in metres, and no longer says the breakwater lighthouse's keepers operated the south-end light: the sources say only that it was controlled remotely from the breakwater lighthouse. Sentences that followed LighthouseFriends or Rowlett wording closely were rewritten.
